<subject>Accomplishments for the First Six Months of 2025</subject>
<body>
My accomplishments for the first six months of 2025 include the following:

1.    Rosie New Manufacturing Compliance Forms -- provided essential legal expertise and intellectual input to revise the manufacturing compliance documents to align closely with the aerospace supplier quality standards.

2.   Rosie Wood and Contractual Risk Strategy in the AeroDyn Restructuring -- led the legal and contracts team across all Kestrel business units in reducing Kestrel’s exposure to financial and contractual risks. This involved a rapid assessment of Kestrel’s positions and cross-unit coordination to determine the best course of action to terminate and then value all AeroDyn contracts.

3.    Implemented New Document Retention Policy for AeroCore Systems -- spearheaded the resolution of critical document retention challenges and rolled out a new policy across all divisions within Kestrel.

4.    Thought Leader on Stanley Risk Management -- continued to develop legal frameworks for improved identification and reporting of legal risks throughout Kestrel. Stanley James and the legal risk rating system are key examples. These risk policies have now been applied in Bristol and the Manufacturing unit to better assess and manage legal exposures in those areas.

5.     Developing New Business Areas -- played an integral role in launching new initiatives in composite materials, precision machining, and aerospace electronics by drafting compliance forms and designing innovative ways to manage legal risks.

6.     Deal Machine -- managed projects with numerous complex elements, including the LV Aero Cogen II, Bristol Assembly Line, Aerotech Dynamics, Skybolt Engineering, and AeroTech Fabrications.

7.     Management -- continued to strengthen a deal-focused legal team that understands the core aerospace manufacturing business.

8.     New Generation of Master Agreements -- leading efforts with the Aerospace Industry Standards Association (AISA) to develop the next generation of master contracts that would cover all aerospace component trades, whether physical or financial. This aims to halve the legal workload.
</body>
